videos.title: Split & Rip Sprint Drill with Tony Holler
videos.publisher: Tony Holler / Championship Productions, hosted by Coaches Insider
videos.matchNotes: Use the two-point standing start portion for stance and first-step reference. The page also covers three- and four-point starts and a specific arm drill; PoseTek films a static split stance, controlled 10 m acceleration and clear slowing area, with no floor start.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Playing in the Tunnel — Teaching Lateral Shuffle
videos.matchNotes: Open the linked Teaching Lateral Shuffle video. It illustrates lateral posture and controlled recovery with resistance. PoseTek uses no resistance: shuffle 3 m without crossing the feet, shorten the final steps and stop balanced. Film that braking finish separately.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Curved sprint with a lower load of centrifugal force — Video 1
videos.matchNotes: Use Video 1, the introductory larger-radius curved sprint, as the movement reference. PoseTek specifies a gentle 15 m arc, gradual speed build and clear runoff. Do not copy the smaller-radius, weighted-vest or ball-reaction progressions later on the page.
videos.verification: Publisher video description checked; linked Vimeo player played publicly without sign-in and a curved-running frame was inspected. Full playback not reviewed.

videos.title: How to Control the Soccer Ball out of the Air
videos.matchNotes: Use the laces/instep cushioning demonstration and low solo toss progression. PoseTek drops from around waist height, softens the receiving leg and settles the ball within one step; it does not require a high toss, foot stall or partner service.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: How to Juggle a Soccer Ball
videos.matchNotes: Use the second exercise: drop, allow a bounce, lift with the instep and allow another bounce between touches. This matches the drill's movement; film low, controlled touches below waist height and the catch/reset option, not the later continuous juggling progression.
videos.verification: Video page and published transcript checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: 1 Touch Technique - Right Outside Foot
videos.matchNotes: Reference the outside-foot contact and controlled pass through the cones. This example uses one-touch right-foot passing; PoseTek starts with a stationary ball, uses a wide gate 3–5 m away and repeats on both feet.
videos.verification: Video player, coach attribution and instructions checked in browser; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Hip turn to crossover step — Video 21
videos.matchNotes: Go to Video 21, Hip turn to crossover step. Use the hip opening and crossover as the reference. PoseTek begins side-on and then accelerates forward for 8 m on a planned signal; it does not add the article's reactive basketball task.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Cutting tree - 135 degree cut
videos.matchNotes: Use this explicitly labeled 135-degree cutting-tree demonstration for the sharper direction change. The coach demonstrates on grass using cones. PoseTek uses a short controlled approach and one planned cut back toward the start-side diagonal, then a short exit and reset. Confirm the 135-degree travel-direction change in the filming layout; do not substitute a shallow 45-degree turn or copy a faster approach.
videos.verification: Video title and publisher checked in browser; playback access and sampled demonstration frames checked. No published description; not reviewed frame by frame.

videos.title: Crossover Step (Videos) — movement combinations
videos.matchNotes: Use the training example identified on the page as Sandra's movement combinations, particularly the shuffle/crossover changes. The page distinguishes these from turning fully to run. PoseTek films a planned 3 m shuffle into 5 m of lateral crossover travel while facing forward, without an opponent or basketball.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Control a Soccer Ball with your Thigh
videos.matchNotes: Use the low solo-toss thigh cushioning demonstration. PoseTek raises the thigh early, lowers it on contact and adds a settling foot touch; keep the toss just above thigh height and omit harder partner service.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Soccer Skills: The Drag-Back
videos.matchNotes: Use only the initial sole-on-ball backward roll as a contact reference. The demonstrated move keeps possession and exits in a V; PoseTek instead releases the roll as a gentle layoff to a partner 2–3 m diagonally behind. Film the rear-space check, pass release and movement for the return; do not copy the V-turn.
videos.verification: Video page and published transcript checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: The Art of the Futsal Toe Poke: Full Guide with Tips and Training Drills
videos.matchNotes: Open Andre Caro's linked tutorial for toe-contact technique. It covers several futsal situations; PoseTek films a short, low-power toe poke from close range into a wide target, no goalkeeper, resetting after each shot rather than copying the full combinations.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Speed drill: Half Kneeling Sprint Start
videos.matchNotes: Matches the half-kneeling start, forward lean and drive through the front foot. Retain PoseTek's comfortable knee pad, controlled first steps, 8 m lane and clear slowing area; the example does not establish the athlete's prescribed volume.
videos.verification: Original academy's video listing, direct YouTube link and drill description checked in browser; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Acceleration + Backpedal + Drop Step Sprint
videos.matchNotes: Reference the backpedal-to-drop-step-to-forward-sprint portion. The title includes an initial acceleration that PoseTek omits: film a controlled 3 m backpedal followed by the planned diagonal 6 m exit and runoff.
videos.verification: Video title, publisher and indexed description checked; direct playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Curved sprint with a lower load of centrifugal force — Video 1
videos.matchNotes: Video 1 supplies the gentle-curve running component only. PoseTek adds a marked transition from an 8 m curve to an 8 m straight, gradually aligning the body without planting for a sharp cut. Film the transition clearly; omit the page's tighter curves and weighted variations.
videos.verification: Publisher video description checked; linked Vimeo player played publicly without sign-in and a curved-running frame was inspected. Full playback not reviewed.

videos.title: How to Chest a Soccer Ball
videos.matchNotes: Use the balanced chest contact and low forward control reference. This demonstration uses a partner toss; PoseTek uses a gentle self-toss below head height, soft chest contact and a ground-settling foot touch. No header or volley return is part of the PoseTek drill.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: How to Kick a Ball: Soccer Shots
videos.matchNotes: Reference the laces contact, firm ankle and body position for keeping the strike down. This is a shooting lesson; PoseTek applies those mechanics to a controlled 8–12 m ground pass through a wide gate, with a low follow-through and non-maximal force.
videos.verification: Video page and published transcript checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: How to Curl a Football
videos.matchNotes: Use the inside-foot contact and curved follow-through as the visual reference. The example is framed as a free kick around a wall; PoseTek films a short angled approach and comfortable close-range curling finish without a wall or goalkeeper, not a long free-kick attempt.
videos.verification: Video page and published transcript checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Sprint-float-sprint demonstration — The Harmony of Relaxation and Repetition in Sport: Part II
videos.matchNotes: Use the embedded sprint-float-sprint video for the change from driving to relaxed running and back. The article discusses long, maximal track efforts; PoseTek uses three 8 m zones at controlled submaximal speed, maintaining relaxed motion in the middle zone and a smooth final increase.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Finding the Gold in Backpedal Training for Performance — Videos 1–3
videos.matchNotes: Use Videos 1–3 for coordinated backward travel and balance. These demonstrate backpedal mechanics, not PoseTek's complete brake-and-hold sequence. PoseTek uses a short clear lane, progressively shorter steps into a balanced stop, then turns and walks back; omit the rotational/reactive progressions.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Crossover Step (Videos) — crossover and return to defensive stance
videos.matchNotes: Use the training movement-combination video for lateral crossovers and returning to a forward-facing stance. PoseTek adds its own controlled 5 m lane and uncrossing, progressively shorter braking steps before holding square. Do not copy a reactive opponent, hard reversal or the article's single-plant stopping progression.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: #17 Soccer Training Session — wall volley / half-volley exercise
videos.matchNotes: Use the wall exercise described in the session's 15–20 minute training block (not a video timestamp), especially its half-volley option just after the bounce. The lesson also uses side volleys. PoseTek films a low self-drop, one bounce and straight instep return to a low wall target, then controls and resets.
videos.verification: Video page and description checked; playback not reviewed.

videos.title: Soccer Techniques: Back Heel
videos.matchNotes: Matches the basic stationary backheel contact. PoseTek adds an explicit check behind, a wide gate about 2 m back and slightly to the side, a gentle pass, and turning to inspect the outcome before retrieving.
videos.verification: Video page and published transcript checked; playback not reviewed.
